title: Eifel beech — terrestrial scan of a single tree (28 m)
description: Terrestrial point cloud from the beech stand in the Eifel (4.4 million points, 27.6 m tall), from the same study as the 360° image. DELIBERATELY WITHOUT INVENTORY MARKERS: at breast height the cloud carries a dense, non-circular mass (32,000 points over 1.8 m, circle-fit residual 29 cm), while the vertically continuous columns give only 11 cm diameter — impossible for a 27.6 m tree. The stem base is evidently poorly sampled, the crown dense. Without the authors' workflow (TreeLS, assignment of points to the target tree) no reliable DBH can be derived here; printing a number would be dishonest. The scene thus shows a limit of the chain: not every single-tree cloud supports an inventory.

source.dataset: Zürcher, R., Zhao, J., Lau, A., Brede, B., Klippel, A. (2023): Advancing Forest Monitoring and Assessment Through Immersive Virtual Reality. Wageningen University & Research.
source.attribution: Zürcher, R., Zhao, J., Lau, A., Brede, B., Klippel, A. (2023): Advancing Forest Monitoring and Assessment Through Immersive Virtual Reality. Wageningen University & Research.
source.hinweis: Single-tree cloud, not a plot; local coordinates without CRS. Panorama and point cloud of the dataset are NOT co-registered.
